digest.component_or_area: GitHub Actions CI / Gerrit Verify workflow
propositions: Ubuntu default-tier jobs occupy 30.2 runner-minutes per Verified run due to redundant work: bridge-cadence test reads and parses workflow YAML 1,440 times instead of once, render_unit calls real Pandoc for 232 units but asserts only cardinality, and AST provenance setup rediscovers parent/caller relationships repeatedly.

Merged remediation eliminated YAML re-parsing from bridge cadence (5.7 runner-minute saving) and reduced Pandoc subprocess duplication in hardening test (immutable legacy oracle), but subsequent Verify runs still average 31m28s end-to-end and 27m56s macOS execution, 88s above the 30-minute target.

Same-change Gerrit Verify runs were delayed 24-25 minutes due to job-level always() predicates preventing cancellation of superseded patchsets; merged change 1792 replaced always() with cancellation-aware status checks to address this infra hold.

The 35-second editor loopback fixture setup (socket.getfqdn blocking) is the sole recurring >30s individual Ubuntu/macOS phase; instrumented runs attribute this to DNS lookup contention rather than editor logic.

Pandoc static-corpus architecture research proposes superseding ADR 0095 to move full real-Pandoc replay (884 units in ~185s) to external-integration weekly schedule while retaining small representative real contracts and golden expected-output fixtures in Verify, but implementation requires explicit ADR supersession and paired before/after measurement.

Repeated per-test git-store fixture construction identified as coverage-neutral optimization opportunity (consensus-backed from prior ticket peculiar-calmy-bubblefish); estimated 75-207 runner-second macOS savings remain pending implementation consensus.
